Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (name clearance) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (inscription); deed executed before a Spanish Notary and published in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 20–23 (formation and notarized deed), 33 (constitutive registration), 62 (payment of capital), 72 (minimum capital), 210–211 (registered office); supplemented by Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece' permitting the Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de Constitución (notarized deed of incorporation) with approved estatutos sociales; registration in the Registro Mercantil is constitutive of corporate personality under LSC Art. 33.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 29 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Standard SL requires EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation (LSC Art. 72); under Ley 18/2022 an SL de Formación Sucesiva may incorporate with a paid-up capital below EUR 3,000 (including EUR 1), subject to a mandatory legal reserve of 20% of annual profits until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached and to restrictions on profit distribution and insolvency filings.

Funding & unlock path: Not applicable for pure digital operations without physical premises. If an office is leased: obtain local fire-safety certification, structural load clearance per the building's occupancy certificate (licencia de primera ocupación), and comply with Ley 31/1995 on occupational risk prevention, including a written PRL risk assessment and workplace safety equipment inspection for any employees.

Paid-in capital rule: Standard SL requires EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation (LSC Art. 72); under Ley 18/2022 an SL de Formación Sucesiva may incorporate with a paid-up capital below EUR 3,000 (including EUR 1), subject to a mandatory legal reserve of 20% of annual profits until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached and to restrictions on profit distribution and insolvency filings.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft

The founder's subscription of the entire share capital (EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 participations of EUR 1.00 each) is ratified, and the bank certificate evidencing full cash payment is annexed. 2. Registered Office. The registered office is fixed at Madrid, Spain; the Board adopts this address and instructs the Secretary to file all statutory registrations. 3. Officers. [Name] is appointed Sole Administrator with all powers granted by law, including opening bank accounts and signing contracts. 4. Compliance. The Board approves the NIF application, tax census filing, and corporate book plan. All resolutions passed unanimously. Certified.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

Not applicable — the activity is a digital audio-licensing marketplace with no manufacturing establishment; it falls outside the scope of Ley 21/1992 de Industria. Only administrative activities under Ley 17/2009 (LSSI) and data-protection rules apply.

Category: Not applicable — no industrial operating permit. Voluntary municipal licencia de apertura/actividad is required only if a physical office is leased; electronic commerce compliance requires the LSSI legal notice and imprint, plus GDPR registration with the Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) where processing subscriber data.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Spanish Tax Administration Agency; electronic portal and online services: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es), accessible via Cl@ve PIN, digital certificate, or Cl@ve permanente.

E-government filing portal

For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (1) Execute public deed of incorporation (escritura pública) before a notary and register with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); (2) Obtain the provisional and then definitive Código de Identificación Fiscal (CIF/NIF) from AEAT; (3) File Modelo 036 (declaration of commencement, modification, or cessation of economic activity) before commencing operations; (4) Non-resident shareholders are permitted without driving registration; if the SL constitutes a permanent establishment of a non-resident entity, the non-resident must appoint a fiscal representative, obtain a NIF-N, and file Modelo 036 with the representative's powers of attorney; foreign entities without a permanent establishment may obtain a NIF through Modelo 036 for pre-incorporation acts or direct VAT registration.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation – The SL is a separate resident taxpayer for Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax, Ley 27/2014, LIS), with worldwide taxation on income and gains for resident companies (resident if incorporated in Spain or having its place of effective management there). General CIT rate: 25% on the full net taxable base; reduced 15% rate for the first two taxable periods for newly created SLs carrying on an active economic activity, applying to a taxable base up to EUR 300,000 per period; non-resident entities with a Spanish permanent establishment are subject to non-resident income tax (IRNR) at 24% with an NT-type taxable base, unless treaty-protected; territorial scope therefore is worldwide for residents and Spanish-source only for non-residents. — For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (1) Execute public deed of incorporation (escritura pública) before a notary and register with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); (2) Obtain the provisional and then definitive Código de Identificación Fiscal (CIF/NIF) from AEAT; (3) File Modelo 036 (declaration of commencement, modification, or cessation of economic activity) before commencing operations; (4) Non-resident shareholders are permitted without driving registration; if the SL constitutes a permanent establishment of a non-resident entity, the non-resident must appoint a fiscal representative, obtain a NIF-N, and file Modelo 036 with the representative's powers of attorney; foreign entities without a permanent establishment may obtain a NIF through Modelo 036 for pre-incorporation acts or direct VAT registration.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation – The SL is a separate resident taxpayer for Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax, Ley 27/2014, LIS), with worldwide taxation on income and gains for resident companies (resident if incorporated in Spain or having its place of effective management there). General CIT rate: 25% on the full net taxable base; reduced 15% rate for the first two taxable periods for newly created SLs carrying on an active economic activity, applying to a taxable base up to EUR 300,000 per period; non-resident entities with a Spanish permanent establishment are subject to non-resident income tax (IRNR) at 24% with an NT-type taxable base, unless treaty-protected; territorial scope therefore is worldwide for residents and Spanish-source only for non-residents.

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a check-the-box or entity-classification election. Available statutory elections/regimes: (a) corporate tax consolidation regime (arts. 55–80 LIS) for groups holding at least 75% of voting capital; (b) ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) regime (art. 107 LIS) for qualifying holding companies of non-resident subsidiaries, granting exemption on qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains; (c) patent/intellectual-property box (art. 23 LIS) allowing reduced effective taxation of eligible intangible-derived income; (d) R&D&I tax credits (art. 35 LIS); (e) lower rate by reinvestment of extraordinary income in new assets; (f) hybrid-mismatch disallowance and deduction-restriction rules implementing ATAD/ATAD2 (arts. 15 bis, 41.1º, 42–43 LIS) – payments arising from hybrid instruments or entities that generate double non-taxation are nondeductible; no voluntary election is available to shift a Spanish SL to pass-through treatment.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No de-minimis turnover threshold for domestic established businesses – any economically active person or company performing taxable supplies in Spain must register in the territorial VAT census (Modelo 036/037) before commencement of activity; the small-business simplified regime (régimen simplificado) is available for qualifying traders with annual turnover up to EUR 250,000 for goods or EUR 150,000 for professional services; distance sales of goods to final EU consumers trigger Spanish registration either directly under the EU OSS system once intra-community distance sales exceed EUR 10,000 per calendar year across the EU-wide threshold.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

0% VAT is available under art. 21 Ley 37/1992 for (a) goods physically dispatched or transported outside the EU customs territory, including Ceuta and Melilla, provided the exporter proves physical departure within the statutory 3-month period from dispatch; (b) installations or assembling of goods in non-EU countries; (c) supplies to diplomatic missions and international organisations; (d) services rendered to non-established entrepreneurs (B2B) are outside Spanish VAT by place-of-supply rules (arts. 69–70 Ley 37/1992) – the Spanish supplier applies 0% VAT with the tax chargeable under reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction; royalty-free stock-music licences and audio subscription sales to overseas business customers are therefore zero-rated in Spain only when the customer's entrepreneur status and foreign VAT ID are validated; exports and B2B foreign services may concurrently be excluded rather than zero-rated, both producing refundable input VAT. Documentary evidence must demonstrate destination, customer identity, nature of the supply and payment flow.

  • Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / DUA) with exit-stamped proof of departure from the EU customs territory by a Spanish/EU customs authority
  • Bill of Lading (B/L), air waybill, CMR consignment note, or other international transport document showing destination outside Spain and the EU
  • Commercial invoice and underlying licensing/subscription agreement identifying the overseas customer (legal name, country of establishment, and VAT identification number or equivalent non-VAT identifier)
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 credit confirmation evidencing receipt of payment in a Spanish bank account from the non-resident buyer
  • Copy of the customer's VAT ID (VAT Information Exchange System validation printout for EU customers) supporting the B2B place-of-supply analysis
  • Inventory/warehouse dispatch notes and packaging lists for physical exports, plus certificates of origin where applicable

AEAT does not apply real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping (no Verifactura-style control). Instead: (1) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) – mandatory real-time submission of VAT invoice books through machine-to-machine XML web services for taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000 and for certain special-scheme taxpayers; (2) Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) – B2B electronic invoicing is phased in (2024–2026) for all entrepreneurs, requiring interoperable e-invoices in Facturae, CII (Cross-Industry Invoice) or UBL formats with digital signature; (3) Standard periodic declarative duties: quarterly Modelo 303 (monthly for SII-affected taxpayers) and annual Modelo 390; Modelo 349 (Recapitulative Sales List) for intra-community goods supplies and EU services; all invoices must include the issuer/recipient NIF, full descriptors, serialised invoice number, taxable base, applicable VAT rate and total tax.

AEAT may reopen and claw back the 0% export treatment for up to 4 years from the termination of the relevant VAT period (Art. 66 Ley General Tributaria, LGT); a supplementary assessment with late-payment interest will be raised if the documentary bundle is incomplete, if the exported goods return into the EU, or if payment is not received within the audited period. Sanctions under Ley General Tributaria arts. 191–207 range from 50% (negligence) to 150% (concealment or repeated infractions) of the undue VAT amount, scaled upward by 50% where tax-avoidance intent is proven; criminal tax fraud under art. 305 Código Penal applies where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per year, carrying penalties of up to 6 years imprisonment and fines up to six times the defrauded amount. Particular audit focus is placed on proof of physical exit, invoice date versus VAT period allocation, customer identity validation, and unexplained payment delays exceeding 180 days which rebut export bona fides.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain maintains full capital and current account convertibility as part of the eurozone and EU obligation under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no general exchange controls or approval requirements for inbound or outbound investment, debt, dividends, interest, or royalty payments. Profit remittance is unrestricted, but cross-border transfers must be reported for statistical purposes via the Banco de España (e.g., forms for external investment declarations) and are subject to standard withholding taxes on dividends and royalties (typically 19% under domestic law unless reduced by an applicable double tax treaty). Dividend distributions and royalty payments must be supported by adequate economic substance and compliance with transfer pricing rules to avoid reclassification or denial of treaty benefits. Repatriation of capital from an SL is tax-free up to the contributed capital base, provided the capital redemption is formally executed via notarial deed and registered at the Mercantile Registry; excess is treated as distributable profit subject to withholding tax.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Spain. Exporters may freely retain, use, or convert euro or foreign currency proceeds. Receipts from cross-border sales of royalty-free music licenses are treated as export proceeds and must be declared in the annual commercial accounts and for corporate income tax purposes; they are also subject to statistical reporting to Banco de España where the transaction threshold is met (typically EUR 50,000 or more). The invoicing, payment method, and underlying license agreement must be retained for AML/KYC and tax audit evidence, but no timeline for forced conversion exists.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting under the framework of the European System of Central Banks and in coordination with the European Central Bank; foreign investment notification and statistical monitoring are managed by the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business) and the Banco de España

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Moderate to High, subject to legal limitations. Spanish-law financial tech entities must be authorized as Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) by the Banco de España or passported from another EU Member State under the EEA passport regime. Such EMIs can legally offer cross-border payment accounts, IBANs, commercial settlement, and EUR SEPA/instant clearing, but they are not deposit-taking banks and are not eligible for the Bank of Spain deposit guarantee scheme. A standard Spanish SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) can open an account with an authorized EMI; however, EMI platforms generally impose lower transaction caps, stricter source-of-funds verification for B2B payments, and may not support complex FX hedging or trade finance (documentary letters of credit). For the royalty-free stock music business, EMIs are adequate as a supplementary collection rail but should not replace a Tier-1 Spanish credit institution as the primary treasury anchor.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident shareholders in a low-tax or blacklisted jurisdiction (e.g., a Panamanian or Belizean parent or shell shareholder)

Root cause: Non-resident shareholders in a low-tax or blacklisted jurisdiction (e.g., a Panamanian or Belizean parent or shell shareholder)

Defense evidence: A complete written and evidenced ownership chain, the SLE incorporation documentation, a notarised certificate of good standing of the non-resident entity, audited financial statements or the parent's latest annual return, signed declarations concerning tax residence and CFC/controlled foreign company status, and an explanation letter confirming commercial operational substance in Spain
Disproportionate volume of cross-border incoming payments from multiple foreign digital marketplaces (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, audio libraries) with no visible supply chain or payroll

Root cause: Disproportionate volume of cross-border incoming payments from multiple foreign digital marketplaces (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, audio libraries) with no visible supply chain or payroll

Defense evidence: Validated license distribution agreements with marketplaces, an automated royalty reporting ledger showing monthly usage and payment allocation, issuer invoices or licensee statements addressed to the Spanish SL, and documented corporate income tax (IS) accrual records including an estimate of digital VAT/GST processing
High-value transactions with no economic explanation or discrepancy between invoice amount and actual payment received

Root cause: High-value transactions with no economic explanation or discrepancy between invoice amount and actual payment received

Defense evidence: Time-stamped license contracts, a detailed price list for royalty-free audio tiers, delivery proof (e.g., watermarking key issuance or download URL access log), and multi-bank source-of-funds evidence showing the remitter is contractually identical to the counterparty named in the underlying license
Immediate withdrawals of funds from an operational account to a personal account or a third-country account following credits from licence marketplaces

Root cause: Immediate withdrawals of funds from an operational account to a personal account or a third-country account following credits from licence marketplaces

Defense evidence: Formal dividend approval minutes signed by the sole shareholder or board, tax advisory evidence validating withholding and capital tax rules, payment to a named distribution account covered by intercompany agreement or shareholder loan agreement, and maintained books and records evidencing that the SL has sufficient distributable reserves
One-time or recurring related-party payments for 'management' or 'intellectual property' services without tangible documentation

Root cause: One-time or recurring related-party payments for 'management' or 'intellectual property' services without tangible documentation

Defense evidence: Transfer-pricing-consistent contract (including TPM for copyright licences), fee structure based on an arm's length benchmark, recipient entity accounts and a signed declaration of tax residency, evidence of actual operational performance (e.g., project reports, task logs, email exchange with a professional domain), and a certificate that no permanent establishment has been created without registration

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

For contributions by non-resident shareholders to the Spanish SL capital (i.e., an increase of capital or payment of the shareholding premium), the legally compliant route includes a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the shareholder's own bank account with the payment purpose coded as 'Capital Contribution – Capital Increase' (Code G? Use of the European Bank Payment Standard to describe the transaction is acceptable; the sending bank should apply a corporate/MF purpose 'Capital contribution' or 'Investment in equity of non-financial corporation'). The contribution must be channelled through a Spanish bank account in the SL's name. The company must file a foreign investment declaration form (Form D-6 for direct investment notifications – 'Declaración de Inversión Exterior Directa') with the Spanish Trade Office (Secretaría de Estado de Comercio) where the contribution exceeds EUR 1,000,000, or if the non-resident participation reaches 10% or more; even below these thresholds, statistical reporting is generally required. The bank will require an executed capital increase deed (public deed by notary), the relevant registration in the Mercantile Registry, the NIF certificate, and the SL's corporate bank signatory mandate. The capital contribution must be credited to a separate 'capital increase' sub-account or clearly designated, and the SL must issue a capital certificate reflecting the new UBO ownership. Evidentiary verification includes bank statements showing the contributory remitter matches the shareholder name, the purpose code, and the shareholder statement confirming no third-party financing (or in the case of a shareholder loan, a separate compliant intercompany loan agreement).Cross-border settlements with trade counterparties and licensors should be performed using standard SWIFT rails. Payments to foreign licensees or suppliers under EUR-denominated contracts within the SEPA zone can use SEPA Credit Transfer (instant SEPA where available). For outside-EEA jurisdictions, SWIFT MT103 is the standard robust clearing rail, requiring the full beneficiary name, IBAN or account number, BIC/SWIFT code, and accurate payment purpose codes (Spain's EBA/BPR standard e.g., 'NDC' – non-dividend distribution of profit; for royalty payments use 'ROYL' – royalty). Where the SL purchases, licences or commissions sound recordings from producers outside the EU, commercial payment is supported by documentary collection (e.g., SWIFT MT544/547 forms in association with a standby LC) or by an irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit (UCP 600) from a Spanish issuing bank naming the producer as beneficiary. In all outbound trades, the SL must retain underlying commercial invoices, license agreements, and a bank reference for the payment to pass internal anti-economic-sanctions screening; if transaction value exceeds EUR 10,000 when involving a third country, additional tax reporting may be triggered under the Spanish annual tax reporting on foreign operations (Modelo 720) for owners. Non-derivative outbound disbursements are not subject to FX control, but the SL is responsible for embargo/sanctions compliance under EU Regulation 833/2014 and ISCI protocols.EUR/USD forward outright contracts with a licensed Spanish bank or EU/EEA investment firm (available for up to 1-2 year tenors, dependent on credit line)EUR/GBP forward outright contracts for the typical UK/US music licensing marketNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offered by Spanish bank desks with maturity and fixing based on reference rates, subject to legal ISDA documentation and physical settlement restrictions when underlying exposure is a non-convertible currencyCross-currency swaps for EUR/major non-EU currency streams, executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with collateral or margin agreement, used for cash flow restructuringCurrency options (EUR call/foreign put or EUR put/foreign call) for hedging the proceeds of large license distributions, available only when the SL has a demonstrated current balance-sheet exposurePlain-vanilla FX swaps (swaps of principal and interest in two currencies) for the SL's temporary liquidity mismatch between receivable and payable accounts

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Moderate to High, subject to legal limitations. Spanish-law financial tech entities must be authorized as Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) by the Banco de España or passported from another EU Member State under the EEA passport regime. Such EMIs can legally offer cross-border payment accounts, IBANs, commercial settlement, and EUR SEPA/instant clearing, but they are not deposit-taking banks and are not eligible for the Bank of Spain deposit guarantee scheme. A standard Spanish SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) can open an account with an authorized EMI; however, EMI platforms generally impose lower transaction caps, stricter source-of-funds verification for B2B payments, and may not support complex FX hedging or trade finance (documentary letters of credit). For the royalty-free stock music business, EMIs are adequate as a supplementary collection rail but should not replace a Tier-1 Spanish credit institution as the primary treasury anchor.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 - Base imponible general Taxable income from ordinary activities For non-residents without PE, income is attributed to PE; adjust for treaty relief Administrative fines €60-€600 per day of delay (max €18,000); criminal penalties for evasion including imprisonment

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: €50,000,000 consolidated group revenue for Master File and Local File requirements

Economic substance scope: Applicable to certain entities (e.g., pure equity holding companies); requires adequate employees, premises, and core income-generating activities in Spain; non-compliance may lead to recharacterization

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax return non-filing or late filing

Statutory sanction: Fines ranging from €60 to €600 per day of delay, capped at €18,000; possible 3-month imprisonment for repeated offenses

Director personal liability: Directors personally liable for tax obligations; potential disqualification from company management and criminal liability
Transfer pricing documentation failure

Statutory sanction: Tax adjustments up to 100% of non-arm's length amount plus interest and fines up to €600,000

Director personal liability: If willful, directors may face criminal charges for tax fraud, including imprisonment and fines
Failure to apply treaty relief or economic substance

Statutory sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, back taxation, fines up to €600,000

Director personal liability: Personal civil and criminal liability in cases of fraud or abuse of rights
